messages:
elaine: Heads up — after last night's network-policy rollout some GPU inference pods in ns=compute-canary lost connectivity to our kv-store in ns=kv-store. Liveness probes failing, RDMA errors in logs.
ram: Oof. Which policy changed?
elaine: The change was a consolidated deny-everything egress policy we applied to reduce blast radius. Here's the relevant policy snippet I applied:```yaml
apiVersion: projectcalico.org/v3
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-clusterwide
spec:
  selector: all()  # intended to be narrow but got broad
  types:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - action: Deny
    ipBlocks:
    - cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
      except:
      - 10.0.0.0/24
```
ram: That ipBlock/except looks suspicious. Are probes coming from 10.0.0.0/24?
maria: Can you tcpdump on a compute-canary pod and on the kv-store side? If it's RDMA (verbs) it may be being blocked at L3/L4.
elaine: tcpdump from a pod:```shell
$ tcpdump -nni eth0 host 10.2.11.7 and port 7500 -c 20
16:02:12.311234 IP 10.2.5.21.7500 > 10.2.11.7.7500: RST, seq 0, win 0, length 0
16:02:12.311567 IP 10.2.11.7 > 10.2.5.21: ICMP net-unreachable
```
sean: Calico log around the time? Maybe deny rule is matching earlier than the intended allow rule.
sre-bot: [alert] NetworkPolicy "deny-egress-clusterwide" created by @elaine at 2026-04-04T01:12:45Z — matched 42 endpoints.
maria: FYI Calico's processing of ipBlock "except" can be surprising when used in a broad Deny policy — the exception is only evaluated after the ipBlock match; if your selector is all() you can still deny traffic originating/forwarded via different nodes. Also policies with broad selectors can affect DNAT/forward path.
ram: So root cause = deny policy was too broad, and the ipBlock except didn't cover probe source CIDR because probes come from hostNIC addresses in different subnets?
elaine: Correct. The kv-store pods live on 10.2.11.0/24 but the kube-proxy/host NAT path used 10.3.0.0/16 for some flows, so traffic never matched the except. We also saw calico dropping on FORWARD chain: "calico: deny outgoing packet: policy=deny-egress-clusterwide src=10.2.5.21 dst=10.2.11.7"
sean: Fix plan?
maria: Quick mitigation: add an explicit allow egress NetworkPolicy scoped to ns=compute-canary that permits podSelector: app=kv-client to dst namespaceSelector: app=kv-store on the ports used (incl. RDMA ports), then revert or narrow the deny policy. Also add hostEndpoint/ASG carve-outs if needed.
elaine: Did that — applied `allow-egress-to-kv` and probes came back within ~30s. Rolling back deny to a namespaced deny that excludes compute-canary while we audit.
ram: Can we add a unit/regression test for any future rollouts that asserts kv-store probe success across namespaces?
maria: Yes — I'll add an e2e that spins up a small client in a target namespace and verifies connectivity after netpols applied. Also adding a checklist: avoid clusterwide selectors with ipBlock=0.0.0.0/0 unless explicitly validated.
elaine: Root cause summary: over-broad deny NetworkPolicy with ipBlock:0.0.0.0/0 + except that didn't match actual host/NAT subnets, which caused east-west pod-to-pod (and RDMA-related) traffic to be dropped. Remediation: scoped deny -> namespace-scoped denies + explicit allow for probe/client namespaces, and added e2e.
sean: Nice catch. Filing follow-up docs + PR to change policy templates. PR: https://git.company/redwood/netpols/pull/432
elaine: TL;DR: don't use clusterwide ipBlock denies unless you enumerate actual host subnets; use namespaceSelector-based policies or explicit allow rules for infra paths. :white_check_mark:
